novel.justification: This support-version regularity is imposed transparently beyond the proceedings paper. It holds, for example, in location-regression data-generating processes \(\Delta Y=g(X,Z)+\varepsilon\) with \(E[\varepsilon\mid X,Z]=0\) and a continuous structural mean on each compact observed component; it does not require zero treatment change to be observed.

assumptions.condition: There is a jointly measurable version such that \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X,Z]=E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X]\) \(Q\)-almost surely for every \(d\in X_0\)

standard.name: conditional parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support

novel.justification: This heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement restriction is substantive and is not inherited from the common-zero-baseline bounded-CAS result. It is satisfied by random-coefficient location models \(Y_2^Q(d)=a(X,U)+c(X,U)d\) with \(|c(X,U)|\le K\) almost surely, and more generally by absolutely continuous dose-response schedules whose individual marginal effects are bounded by \(K\). Such caps are credible for policy doses or temperature exposures over a prespecified compact range.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak Q(P)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak Q(P)=\{Q: Q\text{ is a law over the declared one-argument static schedules},\ m_Q\in C(X_0),\text{ and ass:observed-law-match, ass:consistency, ass:latent-integrability, ass:conditional-parallel-trends, ass:mean-movement-bound, ass:trend-bound, and ass:trend-lipschitz hold}\}\). Thus sharpness is defined over the continuous-trend compatible-completion subclass.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_P\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_P=\{u\in C(X_0): \|u\|_\infty\le M,\ |u(x)-u(x')|\le L|x-x'|\ \forall x,x'\in X_0,\ |g(x,z)-u(x)|\le K|z|\ \forall(x,z)\in H\}\)

definitions.name: affine full-law lift
definitions.construction: \(b_u=\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}/Z,\quad Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=Y_1+b_u(d-D_1),\quad Y_2^{Q_u}(d)=Y_2+b_u(d-D_2),\quad d\in I\), with \(b_u=0\) on the \(P\)-null event \(Z=0\). Then \(Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\) for every \(d\in I\).

definitions.name: worked heterogeneous-baseline completion
definitions.construction: Let \(I=[-1,1]\) and \(K=L=M=1\). The observed law \(P^{\diamond}\) assigns probability \(1/2\) to each of \((Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2)=(0,0,-1/2,0)\) and \((0,0,1/2,0)\). For any function \(u\) on \(\{-1/2,1/2\}\), set \(b_u^{\diamond}=-2u(-1/2)\) when \(X=-1/2\) and \(b_u^{\diamond}=2u(1/2)\) when \(X=1/2\), and define the one-argument schedules of \(Q_u^{\diamond}\) by \(Y_1^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(d)=b_u^{\diamond}(d-D_1)\) and \(Y_2^{Q_u^{\diamond}}(d)=b_u^{\diamond}(d-D_2)\) for \(d\in[-1,1]\), while retaining the observed law \(P^{\diamond}\).

definitions.name: absolutely continuous conditional-support-hole witness
definitions.construction: Fix \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), let \(I=[-2,2]\), and set \(K=L=M=1\). Under \(P^{\circ}\), \(Y_1=Y_2=0\), \(D_1=X\), \(D_2=X+Z\), and \((X,Z)\) has Lebesgue density \(2p_{\circ}\) on \([-1,0]\times[1/2,1]\), density \(2(1-p_{\circ})\) on \([0,1]\times[-1/4,1/4]\), and zero elsewhere. Define \(u_+^{\circ}(x)=\min\{-x,1/2\}\) for \(x\in[-1,0]\) and \(u_+^{\circ}(x)=0\) for \(x\in[0,1]\), and set \(u_-^{\circ}=-u_+^{\circ}\). For \(s\in\{+,-\}\), retain the observed variables under \(P^{\circ}\) and define \(Y_1^{Q_s^{\circ}}(d)=-u_s^{\circ}(X)(d-X)/Z\) and \(Y_2^{Q_s^{\circ}}(d)=-u_s^{\circ}(X)(d-D_2)/Z\) for \(d\in[-2,2]\), with both quotients set to zero on the \(P^{\circ}\)-null event \(Z=0\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal C_P^{\varepsilon}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_P^{\varepsilon}=\{v\in C(X_0):\|v\|_\infty\le M,\ |v(x)-v(x')|\le L|x-x'|\ \forall x,x'\in X_0,\ |g(x,z)-v(x)|\le K|z|+\varepsilon\ \forall(x,z)\in H\}\)

definitions.name: \(\rho_H,H_h,B_h,\pi_h,\nu_{P,h}\)
definitions.construction: \(\rho_H((x,z),(x',z'))=\|(x,z)-(x',z')\|_\infty\) when the two points are in the same connected component of \(H\), and \(\rho_H=+\infty\) otherwise. The finite set \(H_h\subset H\) obeys \(\sup_{w\in H}\min_{w_j\in H_h}\rho_H(w,w_j)\le h\); \(B_h=\{d:(d,z)\in H_h\}\). A Borel nearest-node map \(\pi_h:X_0\to B_h\) satisfies \(|x-\pi_h(x)|\le h\), with deterministic tie-breaking, and \(\nu_{P,h}=(\pi_h)_\#\nu_P\).

definitions.name: \(\ell_{P,h},r_{P,h},\mathcal C_{P,h},e_h,\bar e_h\)
definitions.construction: \(\ell_{P,h}(x)=\max\{-M,\max_{(d,z)\in H_h}[g(d,z)-K|z|-L|x-d|]\}\), \(r_{P,h}(x)=\min\{M,\min_{(d,z)\in H_h}[g(d,z)+K|z|+L|x-d|]\}\), \(\mathcal C_{P,h}=\{v\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(v)\le L,\ \ell_{P,h}\le v\le r_{P,h}\}\), \(e_h=\max\{\|\ell_P-\ell_{P,h}\|_\infty,\|r_{P,h}-r_P\|_\infty\}\), and \(\bar e_h=(K+L)h+Gh^\beta\).

definitions.name: finite inner and outer endpoint programs
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal U_h^{\mathrm{out}}=\{v\in\mathbb R^{B_h}:|v(x)|\le M,\ |v(x)-v(x')|\le L|x-x'|,\ |g(d,z)-v(d)|\le K|z|\ \forall(d,z)\in H_h\}\). Let \(E_hv\) be the deterministically tie-broken bounded McShane extension of \(v\) to \(X_0\), and set \(\mathcal U_h^{\mathrm{in}}=\{\Pi_P(E_hv):v\in\mathcal U_h^{\mathrm{out}}\}\), \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{out}}(v)=\int v\,d\nu_{P,h}=\sum_{x\in B_h}v(x)\nu_{P,h}(\{x\})\), and \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{in}}(v)=J_P(\Pi_P(E_hv))\). The outer support values optimize \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{out}}\) over the finite polytope; the inner support values optimize \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{in}}\) over the same finite parameter set.

definitions.name: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{P:\text{ass:rectangle-support, ass:density-lower, ass:density-upper, ass:bounded-outcomes, ass:holder-regression, and ass:denominator-separated hold}\}\)

definitions.name: boundary-aware band-to-program handle
definitions.construction: Set \(h_n=\{\log(8n/\alpha)/n\}^{1/(2\beta+2)}\) and form a deterministic half-open partition \(\mathscr P_n\) subordinate to the known rectangles, with cell diameter at most \(h_n\), cell area at least \(h_n^2/8\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), no cell crossing a connected component, and deterministic boundary assignment. Let \(\widehat g_n\) be the cellwise mean of \(\Delta Y\), set equal to zero on an empty cell, with \(r_n=Gh_n^\beta+2B\sqrt{128\log(8N_n/\alpha)/(nf_0h_n^2)}\). Set \(\widehat\nu_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nS_i\delta_{X_i}\), \(q_n=2(2M+L\operatorname{diam}(X_0))\sqrt{\log(8/\alpha)/(2n)}\), \(\widehat T_n=n^{-1}\sum_iS_i\Delta Y_i\), \(\widehat A_n=n^{-1}\sum_i|Z_i|\), \(t_n=4B\sqrt{\log(16/\alpha)/(2n)}\), and \(a_n=\operatorname{diam}(I)\sqrt{\log(16/\alpha)/(2n)}\). Choose a deterministic component-respecting \(s_n\)-net with \(s_n\le h_n\), and let \(\widehat B_n\) contain its baseline projections and every observed \(X_i\). The polytope \(\widehat{\mathcal U}_n^{\mathrm{out}}\subset\mathbb R^{\widehat B_n}\) imposes \(|v(x)|\le M\), all pairwise \(L\)-Lipschitz inequalities, and \(|\widehat g_n(d_j,z_j)-v(d_j)|\le K|z_j|+r_n\) at every support-mesh point. Define \(\widehat{\mathscr F}_n=\{(v,j,t,a):v\in\widehat{\mathcal U}_n^{\mathrm{out}},\ |j-\int v\,d\widehat\nu_n|\le q_n,\ |t-\widehat T_n|\le t_n,\ |a-\widehat A_n|\le a_n,\ a\in[a_0,\operatorname{diam}(I)]\}\). When this set is nonempty, apply the Charnes--Cooper transformation and select the lexicographically least optimizer of each of the two resulting linear programs; their clipped objective values are \(\widehat L_n=\max\{-K,\inf_{(v,j,t,a)\in\widehat{\mathscr F}_n}(t-j)/a\}\) and \(\widehat U_n=\min\{K,\sup_{(v,j,t,a)\in\widehat{\mathscr F}_n}(t-j)/a\}\). If the feasible set is empty or these clipped values cross, reset \(\widehat L_n=-K\) and \(\widehat U_n=K\). Define \(\widehat{\mathrm{CI}}_n=[\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\).

definitions.name: \(\mathcal E_n(P)\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E_n(P)=\{\sup_{w\in H}|\widehat g_n(w)-g(w)|\le r_n,\quad \sup_{u\in\mathcal C_P}|\int_{X_0}u\,d(\widehat\nu_n-\nu_P)|\le q_n,\quad |\widehat T_n-T|\le t_n,\quad |\widehat A_n-A|\le a_n,\quad (u|_{\widehat B_n},J_P(u),T,A)\in\widehat{\mathscr F}_n\ \forall u\in\mathcal C_P\}\).

definitions.name: support-hole minimax handle
definitions.construction: Construct Le Cam two-point and Assouad families by placing bounded Hölder perturbations of \(g\) inside a shrinking baseline-specific conditional-support hole and pairing them with opposite signed masses in \(\nu_P\), while keeping pairwise Kullback--Leibler divergence bounded; use the induced separation of the two optimized WAOSS endpoints to study minimax excess length across the point-to-set transition.

statements.statement: Under the observed-law conditions and source-compatible parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support \(X_0\), the continuous-trend compatible-completion subclass \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever these sets are nonempty, \(\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}=\Theta(P)\). For every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), the affine one-argument static-schedule lift produces \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), preserves the entire joint law \(P\), satisfies \(m_{Q_u}=u\in C(X_0)\), and makes both period schedules individually \(K\)-Lipschitz. Moreover, \(Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\) for every \(d\in I\), so the constructed witness satisfies the stronger all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality even though the maintained source condition is required only on \(X_0\), and \(\theta(Q_u)=(T-J_P(u))/A\). This is a strict partial-identification extension of the 2024 proceedings Theorem 1 weighted WAOSS formula: it remains sharp when baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support fails and specializes to that singleton formula under the stronger baseline-conditional support regime. No equality with a broader discontinuous-trend completion class is asserted.
statements.justification: This is the causal kernel: it replaces an unsupported conditional limit by a two-sided, full-observed-law sharp characterization.
statements.gap: Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) imposes only \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta)>0\), while the Appendix proof of Theorem 1 invokes \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta\mid D_1)>0\) immediately before display (4). Under the source's parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support, the present theorem repairs the marginal-support claim with a sharp full-law set. Assumption 5 of de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1) supplies an analogous baseline-conditional support regime, but its Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
statements.consumer: Applied continuous-dose DiD analyses with changing temperatures can report a robustness set without imposing a parametric extrapolation across baseline-specific support holes.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), then \(\mathcal C_P\) is compact and convex in \(C(X_0)\), the extrema \(V_P^-\) and \(V_P^+\) are attained, and \(\Theta(P)=[(T-V_P^+)/A,(T-V_P^-)/A]\subseteq[-K,K]\).
statements.justification: Attainment turns an abstract image into reportable sharp endpoints and rules out closure-only bounds.
statements.gap: Finite-support shape-restriction results attain LP endpoints, but the present feasible object is a continuous function constrained by support-local cones.
statements.consumer: Endpoint attainment supplies explicit least-favorable causal completions for robustness reporting and specification diagnostics.

statements.statement: The envelopes satisfy \(\mathcal C_P=\{u\in C(X_0):\operatorname{Lip}(u)\le L,\ \ell_P\le u\le r_P\}\), and \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(\ell_P(x)\le r_P(x)\) for every \(x\in X_0\).
statements.justification: The result converts latent-model compatibility into an observable necessary-and-sufficient envelope test.
statements.gap: Existing conditional-moment methods provide general tests, but no exact obstacle certificate for these coupled baseline-specific cones.
statements.consumer: Researchers can distinguish rejection of the maintained bounded-trend model from mere failure of point identification.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), then WAOSS is point identified if and only if \(\Theta(P)\) is a singleton, if and only if \(V_P^+=V_P^-\), if and only if \(R(P)=0\).
statements.justification: This corollary records the exact singleton condition implied by the attained endpoint formula and is not presented as an independent diagnostic or novelty claim.
statements.gap: The published conditional-support results give sufficient singleton regimes; this algebraic corollary only records when the new sharp interval collapses.
statements.consumer: Researchers can report whether the computed sharp obstacle interval is a singleton without attributing additional identifying content to a reparameterized width condition.

statements.statement: The family \(P^{\circ}\), indexed by \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), has an \((X,Z)\)-marginal density bounded and strictly positive on its finite rectangle support and uniformly bounded observed outcomes. It satisfies the marginal quasi-stayer part of Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024), while baseline-conditional positivity \(P(|Z|\le\eta\mid X)>0\) fails throughout \([-1,0)\), a baseline region of probability \(p_{\circ}\). The displayed laws \(Q_+^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}\) share \(P^{\circ}\), satisfy the source's Assumptions 1--4, including parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support, and in fact satisfy the stronger all-\(I\) equality because their period difference is dose-invariant. They have different WAOSS values. Therefore the Appendix step immediately before display (4) does not follow from the proceedings paper's marginal Assumption 4.
statements.justification: A regular region, rather than a hand-tuned atom, establishes that the support defect has substantive identifying consequences.
statements.gap: Theorem 1 of the proceedings paper states identification under Assumptions 1--4, but Assumption 4 is marginal and its Appendix proof invokes stronger baseline-conditional positivity immediately before display (4). The explicit conditional support regime in arXiv:2201.06898v1 handles the point-identified case, not the full-law sharp set on the positive-mass failure region exhibited here.
statements.consumer: Users of the published WAOSS estimator obtain an exact support diagnostic identifying when its nonparametric formula remains justified.

statements.statement: Let \(M_{\delta}=\mathbf 1\{|Z|>\delta\}\), and suppose \(P(M_{\delta}=1\mid X)<1\) almost surely for every \(\delta>0\), so thresholds with empty mover events are harmless. This baseline-conditional support condition parallels Assumption 5 in de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1). Under compatibility, the declared continuous support version of \(g\), and parallel trends on \(X_0\), it implies \(\mathcal C_P=\{x\mapsto g(x,0)\}\), \(R(P)=0\), and \(\Theta(P)=\{[T-\int g(x,0)\,d\nu_P(x)]/A\}\). This weighted WAOSS singleton recovers the quasi-stayer-limit formula in Theorem 1 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) under the stronger baseline-conditional support condition. Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 is an analogous conditional-support result for the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\); this proposition does not claim to nest that estimand. Failure of baseline-conditional support on a set of baseline values having positive \(P\)-probability can yield \(R(P)>0\) and a non-singleton \(\Theta(P)\).
statements.justification: The nested corollary separates the proceedings paper's weighted WAOSS formula from the earlier manuscript's analogous unweighted \(\delta_1\) result and locates the new partial-identification region.
statements.gap: The proceedings paper gives the weighted WAOSS quasi-stayer formula, while arXiv:2201.06898v1 Assumption 5 and Theorem 3 concern a conditional-support route to the distinct unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\). Neither gives the sharp weighted WAOSS set when baseline-conditional support fails.
statements.consumer: Researchers can use one support diagnostic to decide whether to report the published singleton formula or the sharp obstacle interval.

statements.statement: At \(P=P^{\diamond}\), the declared objects satisfy \(X_0=\{-1/2,1/2\}\), \(H=\{(-1/2,1/2),(1/2,-1/2)\}\), \(g=0\), \(A=1/2\), \(T=0\), and \(\nu_P=\tfrac12\delta_{-1/2}-\tfrac12\delta_{1/2}\). The obstacle endpoints are \(\ell_P(-1/2)=\ell_P(1/2)=-1/2\) and \(r_P(-1/2)=r_P(1/2)=1/2\), so \(\mathcal C_P=\{u:|u(-1/2)|\le1/2,\ |u(1/2)|\le1/2\}\) and \(\Theta(P)=[-1,1]\). For every such \(u\), the displayed schedules of \(Q_u^{\diamond}\) preserve \(P^{\diamond}\), satisfy \(|b_u^{\diamond}|\le1\), obey parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and, because their period difference is \(u(X)\) at every dose, also obey the stronger all-\(I\) equality, have \(m_{Q_u^{\diamond}}=u\), and attain \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=u(1/2)-u(-1/2)\). The endpoint assignment \(u(-1/2)=1/2,u(1/2)=-1/2\) gives \(b_u^{\diamond}=-1\) and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=-1\); reversing the two signs gives \(b_u^{\diamond}=1\) and \(\theta(Q_u^{\diamond})=1\). This is a heterogeneous two-point baseline design with both signs of treatment change, not the common-zero-baseline scalar design.
statements.justification: The calculation makes the non-singleton frontier and its full-law attainment visible in the smallest genuinely heterogeneous-baseline design.
statements.gap: The common-zero-baseline bounded-slope interval in de Chaisemartin et al. (2024) has one baseline and one scalar nuisance; this example has two baselines, opposite change signs, a signed objective, and distinct affine completions.
statements.consumer: The worked law is a unit test for endpoint software and a transparent template for explaining support-driven partial identification in applications.

statements.statement: For every \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), the \((X,Z)\)-marginal of \(P^{\circ}\) is absolutely continuous with density bounded and strictly positive on each of its two support rectangles, while observed outcomes are bounded, exact stayers have probability zero, and marginal quasi-stayers exist. Conditional quasi-stayer support fails for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), a baseline region of probability \(p_{\circ}\). The observed objects are \(X_0=[-1,1]\), \(H=[-1,0]\times[1/2,1]\cup[0,1]\times[-1/4,1/4]\), \(g=0\), \(A=(1+5p_{\circ})/8\), \(T=0\), and \(d\nu_P(x)=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}dx\). The obstacle envelopes equal \(r_P(x)=-\ell_P(x)=\min\{-x,1/2\}\) on \([-1,0]\) and vanish on \([0,1]\), yielding \(\Theta(P^{\circ})=[-3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ}),3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})]\). The displayed affine laws \(Q_+^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}\) both belong to the continuous-trend legal completion class, preserve the entire observed law, and satisfy parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and the stronger all-\(I\) equality because their period differences are respectively \(u_+^{\circ}(X)\) and \(u_-^{\circ}(X)\) at every dose. They satisfy the new conditional mean-movement bound and attain respectively \(-3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\) and \(3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\).
statements.justification: The positive-density family proves that the conditional-support failure and non-singleton frontier persist away from atomic examples, while the two schedules display legal full-law attainment.
statements.gap: The public conditional-quasi-stayer theorem covers the nested singleton regime, and the common-zero-baseline result has scalar geometry; neither supplies an absolutely continuous heterogeneous-baseline support-hole family with two observed-law-equivalent WAOSS values.
statements.consumer: The family is a regular stress test for support diagnostics, obstacle solvers, and sensitivity plots indexed by the mass \(p_{\circ}\) of unsupported baselines.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\), then for every \(\varepsilon\ge0\), \(\Pi_P\) maps \(\mathcal C_P^{\varepsilon}\) into \(\mathcal C_P\) and \(\|v-\Pi_P(v)\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\). The constant one is sharp. For every component-respecting mesh, the uniform-norm Hausdorff distance satisfies \(d_H(\mathcal C_{P,h},\mathcal C_P)=e_h\); hence each signed support value over \(\mathcal C_{P,h}\) differs from its full-class counterpart by at most \(\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}e_h\).
statements.justification: Exact clipping replaces uncheckable strict-feasibility and active-set assumptions by a global deterministic stability certificate.
statements.gap: Generic LP perturbation theory begins from a finite program and does not give this constant-one continuum feasibility retraction.
statements.consumer: The certificate makes support gridding auditable and allows conservative endpoint computation even at equality constraints.

statements.statement: For every component-respecting \(h\)-net, \(e_h\le\bar e_h=(K+L)h+Gh^\beta\). The extrema of the finite outer linear objective \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{out}}\) over \(\mathcal U_h^{\mathrm{out}}\) are attained and differ from \(V_P^-\) and \(V_P^+\) by at most \(\bar e_h+Lh\), using \(\|\nu_P\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1\). Every value of \(J_{P,h}^{\mathrm{in}}\) is attained by a member of \(\mathcal C_P\), and the inner objective range is within \(2Lh\) of the full objective range. Consequently the induced inner and outer WAOSS intervals have Hausdorff error at most \(A^{-1}(\bar e_h+2Lh)\). These conclusions hold when rectangle boundaries touch, when a connected component is separated from \(z=0\), and when obstacle constraints bind.
statements.justification: The theorem makes the sharp continuous-support set computable with a certified deterministic error.
statements.gap: Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) start with finite discrete support, while Voronin (2025) analyzes values of programs already finite.
statements.consumer: A software implementation can report sharp WAOSS bounds together with a mesh certificate rather than an undocumented gridding tolerance.

statements.statement: Sanity check: When \(P(X=0)=1\) and \(Z>0\) almost surely, the obstacle program collapses to the scalar interval for the common baseline trend and reproduces the bounded-conditional-average-slope WAOSS bounds of de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024).
statements.justification: This reduction is the required sanity check and fixes the boundary between prior art and the varying-baseline contribution.
statements.gap: The scalar common-zero-baseline result is published; the proposition claims equivalence, not novelty.
statements.consumer: Readers can verify that existing heterogeneous-adoption bounds are nested exactly within the new frontier.

statements.statement: For the explicit rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator, signed empirical measure, moment bands, and finite outer program, the lexicographically selected endpoints are Borel measurable and \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}:\,\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing}P\{\mathcal E_n(P)\}\ge1-\alpha\). On \(\mathcal E_n(P)\), every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), together with \(J_P(u)\), \(T\), and \(A\), is feasible through \((u|_{\widehat B_n},J_P(u),T,A)\in\widehat{\mathscr F}_n\), and the empirical endpoints obey \(\widehat L_n\le(T-V_P^+)/A\) and \(\widehat U_n\ge(T-V_P^-)/A\). On the same event both endpoint gaps are nonnegative and each is at most a fixed-class multiple of \(\{r_n+(K+L)s_n+q_n+t_n+Ka_n\}/A\); in particular, signed-measure uncertainty enters as \(q_n/A\) and denominator uncertainty as \(Ka_n/A\). Thus both excess endpoints are \(O(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2})\) uniformly, without density smoothness, strict feasibility, or optimizer uniqueness.
statements.justification: This root inference theorem proves boundary-cell coverage, signed-measure propagation, measurable finite-program endpoints, and the ratio bound on one simultaneous event over compatible laws.
statements.gap: Regression-band, calibrated-projection, and finite LP-value papers each solve only one layer and do not establish their uniform composition for this support geometry.
statements.consumer: The event and endpoint inequalities give empirical WAOSS analyses an auditable route from primitive sampling conditions to honest outer inference.

statements.statement: As an immediate corollary of the simultaneous-event theorem, \(\widehat{\mathrm{CI}}_n=[\widehat L_n,\widehat U_n]\) satisfies \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}:\,\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing}P\{\Theta(P)\subseteq\widehat{\mathrm{CI}}_n\}\ge1-\alpha\). The interval is intersected with \([-K,K]\), and coverage allows \(R(P)=0\), nonunique optimizers, and binding obstacle constraints.
statements.justification: Uniform coverage is the direct reportable consequence of the root inclusion-event and endpoint theorem.
statements.gap: Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) treat finite moment systems, whereas this corollary inherits a primitive uniform boundary-regression and signed-measure inclusion theorem for a continuum completion class. It does not characterize the source paper's separate parametric estimator.
statements.consumer: County-level temperature and other continuously changing policy panels can report one confidence interval covering every full-law-compatible WAOSS value.

statements.statement: Is the uniform excess-endpoint rate \(\{\log n/n\}^{\beta/(2\beta+2)}+n^{-1/2}\) minimax, up to logarithmic factors, over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}\) when baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support can approach failure and \(R(P)\) can approach zero? More sharply, can a matching lower bound distinguish the cost of learning the obstacle boundary from the cost of the signed objective as the identified set changes from a singleton to an interval?
statements.justification: The upper rate becomes economically interpretable only after separating unavoidable support-hole learning from avoidable conservatism in the outer program.
statements.gap: Slow-mover limit theory retains point identification, while calibrated partial-identification inference fixes the identified-set topology; neither supplies a minimax lower bound across this point-to-set transition.
statements.consumer: A matching lower bound would tell practitioners whether shorter uniformly honest WAOSS intervals require stronger support information rather than a different optimizer.

sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed two-period panel sampling from \(P\).
sampling_model.units: Superpopulation units with observed \((Y_1,Y_2,D_1,D_2)\) and static potential-outcome schedules on the known compact interval \(I\).
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous baseline and follow-up doses with no exact stayers; the full-data class imposes source-compatible conditional parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support \(X_0\), while marginal quasi-stayers do not imply baseline-conditional zero support. The constructed affine witnesses satisfy the stronger equality on all of \(I\).
sampling_model.overlap: Population identification allows arbitrary compact observed support \(H\); uniform inference is restricted to a known finite union of rectangles with density between \(f_0\) and \(f_1\) and \(A\ge a_0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A deterministic rectangle-subordinate cell-mean estimator of \(g\) is paired with a signed empirical measure for \(\nu_P\), Hoeffding bands for \(T\) and \(A\), and a component-respecting finite outer ratio program; the root inference theorem controls all ingredients on the single event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\), while population identification itself requires no nuisance estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 1--4, including marginal quasi-stayers in Assumption 4, Theorem 1 states the weighted WAOSS quasi-stayer-limit formula.
In arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1, Assumption 5 imposes baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support, and Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS.
Without quasi-stayers, bounded conditional average slopes yield sharp intersection bounds in the common-zero-baseline design.
The bounds obtained by solving finite linear programs are sharp under the paper's discrete-support shape restrictions.
The data can estimate an upper bound on the diameter of the identified set.
Identified IV-weighted averages restrict policy-relevant weighted averages of the same marginal treatment effects.
Calibrated projection controls coverage uniformly over a large class of moment-inequality models.
Least-squares series estimators admit uniform rates and confidence bands for conditional-mean functionals.
Boundary-adaptive local-polynomial estimators admit uniform Gaussian approximations and confidence bands.
Finite LP-value estimation is pointwise root-\(n\) consistent under feasibility and finiteness.
Bias correction for slow movers yields point-identified panel limit theory under weak treatment changes.

tldr: Under source-compatible parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support, Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) supplies marginal quasi-stayers, while the Appendix proof of its weighted WAOSS formula invokes baseline-conditional positivity immediately before display (4). Assumption 5 and Theorem 3 of arXiv:2201.06898v1 instead give an analogous conditional-support result for the distinct unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\). On the explicitly declared continuous-trend completion subclass and under a new heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement restriction, the full-observed-law sharp WAOSS interval repairs the marginal-support theorem and extends the weighted formula to baseline-specific support holes. A two-period same-slope affine lift realizes every value; its witnesses satisfy the maintained condition on \(X_0\) and the stronger equality on all of \(I\). An absolutely continuous positive-density family has a conditional-support hole and two legal completions attaining different WAOSS values. The root inference theorem places the cell-mean band, signed empirical objective, numerator, and denominator on one uniformly valid event, obtains finite-program endpoint inequalities and the displayed excess rate, and yields honest outer coverage as an immediate corollary.

project_justification.gap: Under parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support, the proceedings paper's Assumption 4 is marginal although its Appendix proof uses baseline-conditional positivity for the weighted WAOSS formula. The earlier manuscript's Assumption 5 explicitly imposes conditional support, but its Theorem 3 identifies the distinct unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\). Neither source characterizes the full-law weighted WAOSS set when baseline-conditional support fails.
project_justification.niche: With heterogeneous baseline doses, observed changes impose support-local cones on a continuous support version of \(g\), while continuous Lipschitz trends enter weighted WAOSS through a signed baseline measure. The same affine slope in both potential-outcome periods preserves observed outcomes and enforces the maintained parallel-trends restriction on \(X_0\), with stronger all-\(I\) validity for the constructed witnesses.
project_justification.fill: The project proves full-law sharpness over the explicitly delimited continuous-trend compatible-completion subclass under source-compatible parallel trends on \(X_0\) and a newly labeled conditional mean-movement restriction. It supplies discrete and absolutely continuous heterogeneous-baseline legal-completion witnesses, the weighted nested-regime reduction to the proceedings formula, clipping geometry, completely defined finite programs, and a root simultaneous-event theorem whose endpoint inequalities and excess rate imply honest outer coverage.

related_work: de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024, Assumption 4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix proof immediately before display (4)) impose parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and state marginal quasi-stayers, but use baseline-conditional positivity in the proof of the weighted WAOSS formula. The sharp-set result repairs that support implication under the same maintained parallel-trends domain without questioning the paper's separate parametric estimator in Section 3. The source chain is distinct from de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1): its Assumption 5 imposes the baseline-conditional Support Condition Without Stayers, while Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS. That theorem is an analogous conditional-support comparator, not an estimand nested by the present result. Under the stronger baseline-conditional support condition, the nested-regime corollary instead recovers the weighted WAOSS singleton formula of the 2024 proceedings Theorem 1; when the condition fails, the full-law theorem supplies the sharp weighted interval. Global continuity of the observed-support version of \(g\) is additional population regularity here, justified by continuous location-regression structural means and not attributed to either source; full-law sharpness is stated only for completions whose baseline trend is continuous and globally \(L\)-Lipschitz. The heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement restriction is also new: it is implied by bounded random-coefficient or bounded-derivative dose-response schedules. The legal affine completion uses the same slope in both period schedules, so its period difference is \(\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\) for every \(d\in I\); thus it satisfies the maintained condition on \(X_0\) and, as a witness property, the stronger all-\(I\) equality. de Chaisemartin, Ciccia, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Knau (2024, Section 4.2.1, Theorem 4, and Appendix B.2 of arXiv:2405.04465v4) give the occupied common-zero-baseline bounded-CAS interval; it appears here only as an algebraic sanity check, with no novelty or strict-tightening claim. The discrete and positive-density rectangle witnesses instead have heterogeneous baselines, support holes, signed obstacle objectives, and explicit two-period affine completions. Freyberger and Horowitz (2015) inform finite shape-restricted linear programs, Freyberger (2017) informs target-image diagnostics, and Mogstad, Santos, and Torgovitsky (2018) informs signed support-function optimization. Belloni et al. (2015) and Cattaneo et al. (2024) inform the simultaneous regression band, while Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) and Voronin (2025) inform optimized-endpoint inference and finite-program stability. Sasaki and Ura (2025) inform the slow-mover side of the minimax point-to-set question but retain point identification. The root inference theorem supplies the missing uniform composition on one event; these papers remain technique ancestors rather than theorem-level targets except where the comparator table records a match.
technical_internal_limitation: The uniform theorem is tied to the explicit known rectangle partition, fixed Hölder exponent, positive density lower bound, and conservative cell-mean radius. It must establish cell occupancy and boundary coverage, signed empirical-process control over the bounded Lipschitz class, measurable finite-program endpoints, and numerator-denominator propagation on the single event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\). It does not establish minimax optimality of the excess-endpoint rate; that question is isolated in the support-hole lower-bound problem.
honest_scope: The population results concern two-period independent sampling, one-argument static potential-outcome schedules on \(I\), known compact treatment support, and the source-compatible condition \(E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X,Z]=E_Q[Y_2^Q(d)-Y_1^Q(d)\mid X]\) for every \(d\in X_0\). The constructed same-slope witnesses satisfy this equality for every \(d\in I\), but stronger all-\(I\) parallel trends are not maintained. A continuous observed-support version of \(g\) is imposed beyond the source assumptions, and sharpness is delimited to compatible completions with continuous globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends. The heterogeneous-baseline conditional mean-movement bound \(K|\Delta D|\) is a new substantive assumption, distinct from the common-zero-baseline paper's bounded-CAS condition; bounded random-coefficient linear schedules are one class satisfying it. Sharpness is not claimed over discontinuous-trend completions. Baseline-conditional support collapses the weighted WAOSS interval to the proceedings paper's formula; arXiv:2201.06898v1 Theorem 3 is only an analogous result for unweighted \(\delta_1\). Outside that regime, point identification is reported only through the algebraic singleton equivalence \(V_P^+=V_P^-\iff R(P)=0\). Hölder regularity, rectangle support, bounded density, bounded outcomes, and denominator separation are confined to the root inference theorem. Honest outer coverage is its immediate corollary. Minimax optimality remains open. No claim is made for carry-over, clustered sampling, unknown support, adaptive smoothness, vanishing \(A\), bounded counterfactual levels, or optimal interval length. The common-zero-baseline scalar bound is prior art and retained only as a sanity check, and the proceedings paper's separate parametric estimator is not invalidated.

seed_details.title: Full-observed-law completion frontier for WAOSS
seed_details.anchor_location: arXiv:2402.05432v1, Assumption 4, Theorem 1, and the Appendix proof immediately before display (4), where baseline-conditional positivity is invoked, were inspected; Section 3 contains the separate parametric estimator.
seed_details.opportunity: Under the source's parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support, replace the unsupported implication from marginal Assumption 4 to the baseline-conditional positivity used immediately before Appendix display (4) by a sharp weighted WAOSS set over an explicitly continuous-trend completion subclass, under a separately labeled heterogeneous-baseline mean-movement restriction, and an observed-law-preserving two-period affine construction.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After conditioning on \(D_1=d\), do not evaluate \(g(d,0)\) unless zero belongs to the corresponding conditional support; retain the support-local cone instead.
seed_details.destination_search: The historical no-stayer section of arXiv:2201.06898v1 gives point identification under explicit baseline-conditional quasi-stayer support; no inspected source gives the varying-baseline signed sharp set when that support inclusion fails.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the source decomposition because one merely replaces a missing limit by an interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial step is constructive full-law sharpness: every feasible trend must be pasted into both static potential-outcome periods while preserving the entire observed joint distribution and satisfying the maintained parallel-trends condition on \(X_0\); the witnesses in fact satisfy the stronger all-\(I\) equality.

seed_details.title: Transport dual for the signed bounded-Lipschitz frontier
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the weighted-functional restriction, the convex-program characterization, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a measure-valued transport dual for the signed WAOSS support function, making cross-baseline cancellation and the cost of Lipschitz coupling explicit.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a positive policy weight by the Jordan decomposition of the signed baseline measure and dualize the two-sided obstacles jointly with Lipschitz transport.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for signed-measure Lipschitz obstacle duals locate general optimal-transport duality but no causal WAOSS formulation or full-law completion result.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Kantorovich duality after writing the Lipschitz constraint.
seed_details.rebuttal: A generic dual is not the causal result; its value depends on first deriving the exact observable obstacles and signed measure from legal full-law completions.

seed_details.title: Certified finite programs for continuous support
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, Proposition 2 and its convex-combination proof, the finite linear programs in equation (6), the endpoint limit theory, and Section 7 were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Convert infinitely many support-local cones and a global Lipschitz restriction into attained finite inner and outer programs with an exact constant-one clipping certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the paper's finite-support vector by obstacle envelopes on a compact support, then prove that mesh feasibility extends and clips back to the continuum class.
seed_details.destination_search: The closest 2025 LP-value work begins with a finite program; no result found supplies the required continuum-to-finite causal certificate on rectangle unions.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by gridding a Lipschitz function and invoking finite LP convergence.
seed_details.rebuttal: Naive gridding gives no inner lift at touching boundaries and no uniform endpoint guarantee under equality constraints; the exact clipping retraction supplies both without Slater conditions.

seed_details.title: Uniform simultaneous-event inference for optimized WAOSS endpoints
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the calibrated relaxation defining projection endpoints, the uniform coverage theorem, the computational algorithm, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Prove uniform probability for the single event \(\mathcal E_n(P)\), simultaneous feasibility of every population trend and objective, finite-program endpoint inequalities, and clipping-based excess-rate propagation.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Before calibrating endpoint optimization, replace finitely indexed moments by a simultaneous band over the observed rectangle support and certify its finite relaxation.
seed_details.destination_search: Calibrated projection treats finite-dimensional moment systems; uniform regression-band papers do not propagate their bands through this support-dependent signed endpoint program.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by feeding a uniform confidence band into a relaxed optimization problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The root theorem must control support boundaries, touching rectangles, nonunique optimizers, and random signed objectives on the same event; no cited component theorem provides that composition.

seed_details.title: Minimax inference across the quasi-stayer point-to-set transition
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the slow-mover bias-correction construction, the distributional theorem, the uniformity discussion, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive the minimax confidence-length frontier as conditional quasi-stayer mass vanishes and support holes open.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Allow the identifying boundary point to leave conditional support, so the local experiment changes from irregular point identification to set identification.
seed_details.destination_search: Slow-mover theory retains point identification, while honest convex-class inference fixes the identified object; no joint topology-changing frontier was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine combination of slow-mover trimming and partial-identification confidence intervals.
seed_details.rebuttal: The local experiment and loss change discontinuously when the target becomes set-valued, so neither existing limit theory transfers directly.

seed_details.title: Boundary-adaptive regression coverage on finite rectangle unions
seed_details.anchor_location: Introduction, the boundary-adaptive local-polynomial construction, the uniform Gaussian approximation, the confidence-band result, and the conclusion were inspected.
seed_details.opportunity: Construct a component-respecting conditional-mean band that remains uniform at outer and touching boundaries and feeds a finite WAOSS program.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Adapt boundary-local polynomial coverage from a conditional-density process to the outcome regression on a known union of support rectangles, without averaging across disconnected components.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found boundary-adaptive density bands and generic series bands, but not the required conditional-mean band coupled to signed partial-identification optimization.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from existing boundary-adaptive local-polynomial confidence bands.
seed_details.rebuttal: As a standalone result the objection largely holds; its only credible role is as a lemma inside the full inference seed.
